item.title: Module: DOCKER
item.description:
Docker is a widely used containerization platform. It provides a standard way to deliver software.

Pigsty provides Docker as an optional module. Pigsty does not require Docker to deploy its components.

Select the Docker software, tool, and application templates that you need. These templates quickly start stateless software in containers to provide extra functions. You can connect these applications to external, highly available database clusters managed by Pigsty.

When you run configure, Pigsty selects suitable upstream repositories and mirror settings from region. For example, it adjusts these settings for networks in mainland China. This improves image download speed and availability.

item.title: Usage
item.description:
Pigsty includes Docker support. Use it to deploy containerized applications quickly.

Getting Started

Docker is an optional module. The docker_enabled parameter controls Docker installation. It is disabled by default.

The docker-ce upstream repository belongs to the infra module. To include Docker packages in the offline repository, set repo_extra_packages to the docker package alias. This alias maps to docker-ce and docker-compose-plugin.

repo_modules: infra,node,pgsql  # <--- Keep infra module (Docker upstream belongs to infra)
repo_extra_packages:
 - pgsql-main
 - docker  # <--- Download Docker (docker-ce + docker-compose-plugin)

After you download Docker, set docker_enabled to true on each target node. Set the other parameters as needed.

item.title: Playbooks
item.description:
The Docker module provides the docker.yml playbook to install Docker Daemon and Docker Compose.

docker.yml

Playbook source file: docker.yml

The playbook installs docker-ce and docker-compose-plugin on target nodes that have docker_enabled: true. It also enables the dockerd service.

The docker.yml playbook has these task subsets:

  • docker_install: Install Docker and Docker Compose packages on the node.
  • docker_admin: Add the specified users to the Docker admin user group.
  • docker_dir: Create Docker directories.
  • docker_config: Generate the Docker daemon service configuration file.
  • docker_launch: Start the Docker daemon service.
  • docker_register: Register the Docker daemon as a monitoring target. Alias tags: register / add_metrics.
  • docker_image: Try to load cached image tarballs from /tmp/docker/*.tgz, if they exist.

The Docker module does not provide a dedicated uninstall playbook. To uninstall Docker, manually stop it and remove it:

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
Who Can Run Docker Commands?

By default, Pigsty adds two users to the Docker operating system group. One is the management user that runs the playbook: the SSH login user on the target node. The other is the admin user specified by node_admin_username. All users in this group (docker) can manage Docker using the docker CLI command.

To let another user run Docker commands, add that OS user to the docker group:
